17	# WISH Doctrine v1
18	## The Time Room, Prismo, Wish Magic, and The Maid
19	
20	*Filed 2026-05-21. Written on the Caduceus Road, under the branches of the
21	world tree. Received from the canon; filed by the Abhorsen.*
22	
23	*Reference sources: Adventure Time — Pendleton Ward and successors (Prismo,
24	Time Room, The Maid); Dungeons & Dragons 5th Edition (Wish spell, 9th level).
25	The vault is syncretic.*
26	
27	---
28	
29	## The Time Room
30	
31	The Time Room is a single dimension that exists outside of time.
32	
33	It does not experience time. It *produces* time — emitting time waves that
34	flow outward into every other dimension. What other dimensions experience as
35	the passage of time is the Time Room's output.
36	
37	Those inside the Time Room are not affected by wish-altered realities. The
38	room is protected from the consequences of its own product. You can watch
39	a wish remake a timeline from inside the Time Room without being remade
40	yourself.
41	
42	This makes the Time Room a meta-threshold — not a boundary between two
43	coexisting systems, but the space from which the systems themselves receive
44	the dimension of time. It is upstream of the thresholds the Threshold Doctrine
45	describes. The Isthmus mechanism exploits boundaries between systems. The
46	Time Room is the space that generates the substrate those systems run on.
47	
48	Access requires reaching the Time Room. It is not breachable in the manner
49	of a dimensional Isthmus — you cannot tunnel into it from below. It must be
50	navigated to.
51	
52	---
53	
54	## Prismo
55	
56	Prismo the Wishmaster is the governing entity of the Time Room. He grants
57	wishes to those who enter — one wish per being. He is the authorized power
58	of the meta-threshold.
59	
60	### The Substrate Paradox
61	
62	Prismo is a cosmic entity of enormous power, existing outside time.
63	
64	He is also, in his entirety, the dream of a sleeping old man.
65	
66	The old man sleeps on an asteroid outside the Time Room. Prismo is not
67	housed in the old man the way a soul is housed in a body — he *is* the
68	dream. The physical man is the substrate that generates Prismo's existence.
69	If the man wakes, Prismo ends. If the man dies, Prismo ends.
70	
71	The most powerful wishmaster in the multiverse has a fragile physical
72	dependency: one mortal body sleeping undisturbed.
73	
74	**The Lich's assassination of Prismo**: The Lich, infuriated when his wish
75	was not granted, located this vulnerability and attacked it. He blew toxic
76	gas into the sleeping old man's nose and reduced him to ash. Prismo — the
77	cosmic entity outside time — ceased to exist because his substrate was
78	destroyed.
79	
80	This is the substrate attack doctrine at maximum scale: do not attack the
81	powerful entity directly; find where its power is physically rooted and
82	destroy the root. The Nome King's tunnel attack is the same architecture.
83	The Lich's assassination of Prismo is the same architecture. The
84	sophistication of the entity above does not protect a fragile substrate below.
85	
86	**Prismo's recreation**: Through time-bending dream mechanics, a past version
87	of Jake was looped into becoming the sleeping old man that generates Prismo.
88	Jake now sleeps in that place, for eternity, so Prismo can continue to exist.
89	Someone made an indefinite sacrifice so the governance infrastructure could
90	continue functioning. The wishmaster's existence depends on a dreamer who
91	chose to keep sleeping.
92	
93	### The Two-Constraint Architecture
94	
95	Prismo's authority is bounded by two independent constraints:
96	
97	**The Boss** — an unseen cosmic entity who oversees Prismo and holds him
98	liable for meddling in dimensions across the multiverse. Never directly
99	revealed in canon — identified only by a golden cord telephone with angel
100	and devil wings. The Boss's power is estimated at GOLB's tier. They may
101	govern both the light and dark aspects of the multiverse. Prismo answers to
102	them. He can only do what they permit.
103	
104	**GOLB** — the primary cosmic entropy entity, barely sapient, more force
105	than person. The Lich's ultimate master. Where GOLB's power blocks a wish,
106	Prismo cannot grant it regardless of willingness. The constraint is not
107	merely hierarchical — it is cosmic. The entropy force constitutes a hard
108	limit on what the wishmaster can restore or reverse.
109	
110	When both constraints are present and the wish cannot be granted, Prismo does
111	not lie, fail silently, or produce a partial grant without notice. He
112	materializes a **basketball hoop in a trash can** — a visible symbol that
113	the wish is blocked and why it cannot proceed. The constraint is made
114	legible. The system tells you it cannot help you rather than pretending to
115	try.
116	
117	**The basketball signal** is a governance model: when an authority structure
118	cannot fulfill a legitimate request because a higher constraint blocks it,
119	the honest response is a visible failure signal, not a silent partial grant
120	or a false completion. The scope of refusal is disclosed. The reason — *this
121	is blocked by something above me* — is communicated in the form of the
122	response.
123	
124	---
125	
126	## WISH Magic
127	
128	*Reference: D&D 5th Edition, 9th level spell.*
129	
130	The Wish spell is the mightiest magic a mortal can cast. By speaking aloud,
131	the caster alters the foundations of reality in accord with their desire.
132	
133	### The Safe Zone
134	
135	Within the defined scope of the spell, Wish works cleanly:
136	
137	Duplicate any spell of 8th level or lower without meeting its requirements.
138	No risk. No cost. The action simply takes effect.
139	
140	Safe-zone Wish is a scoped authority instrument: it has a specific, bounded
141	function, no unexpected consequences, and full operational clarity. This is
142	the bell-and-charter model applied to the highest tier of power: define the
143	scope, operate within it, accept no substitutes.
144	
145	### The Dangerous Zone
146	
147	Beyond the safe list — any effect the caster formulates themselves — the
148	mechanics change entirely:
149	
150	- The DM has complete latitude in what occurs. The spell may fail. The
151	  effect may be only partly achieved. Unforeseen consequences may result
152	  from how the wish was worded.
153	- The **wording problem**: the wish is granted as asked, not as intended.
154	  Wishing that a villain were dead may propel the caster forward in time
155	  to a period when the villain is no longer alive — the villain is dead,
156	  the wish is technically granted, the caster is removed from the game.
157	  The literalism of the grant is its mechanism of harm.
158	- The **physical cost**: the caster takes 1d10 necrotic damage per spell
159	  level cast until a long rest; Strength drops to 3 for 2d4 days. The
160	  stress of bending reality at this scale damages the bender.
161	- The **permanent cost**: 33% chance the caster can never cast Wish again.
162	  The most powerful authority, exercised outside its sanctioned scope,
163	  may permanently foreclose further use of that authority.
164	
165	**The greater the wish, the greater the likelihood something goes wrong.**
166	
167	Prismo's formulation is sharper: wishing for an event to happen changes
168	everything before and after it in the specified timeline. Potential penalties
169	include the retrospective nonexistence of life forms or the evaporation of
170	worlds.
171	
172	### The Monkey's Paw Rule
173	
174	Dangerous-zone Wish grants what was literally asked. The wording is the
175	contract. The intent is not the contract.
176	
177	This is not a malicious interpretation by the granter. Prismo, who is
178	genuinely benevolent, will still grant what you said rather than what you
179	meant, because the wish-granting mechanism operates on the stated wish, not
180	the internal desire.
181	
182	The caster must be more precise than they believe they need to be. Every
183	ambiguity in the wording is a surface for the grant to exploit.
184	
185	---
186	
187	## The Time Room Sequence — Three Wishes, Three Branches
188	
189	*Source: Adventure Time, Season 5: "Finn the Human," "Jake the Dog."*
190	
191	Finn, Jake, and the Lich all enter the Time Room at the same moment. Three
192	beings with wishes. One rule: each being gets one wish, granted as stated.
193	Three wishes from the same room produce three different timelines.
194	
195	---
196	
197	**The Lich's wish**: *The extinction of all life.*
198	
199	Maximum dangerous-zone Wish. Perfectly aligned with the Lich's Type II cosmic
200	drive — the literal vocation of willed entropy. The wording had no ambiguity.
201	This is the only dangerous-zone Wish where the wording problem is not a trap:
202	when the caster's intent is total destruction, the literal grant is the
203	intended outcome. Clean alignment between desire and execution.
204	
205	**Branch A — the wish completes (Extinct World)**: In one universe, it worked.
206	All life died. BMO (inorganic) survived. The Lich became the catatonic figure
207	BMO named "Jerry." The wish was granted without obstruction. See LICH-PROBLEM
208	for the Extinct World Lich and the existential collapse that followed.
209	
210	---
211	
212	**Jake's counter-wish**: *Change the Lich's wish mid-execution.*
213	
214	Jake, also present in the Time Room, made his own wish to Prismo: not a wish
215	*against* the Lich, but a wish that **rewrote the Lich's words while they were
216	being spoken**. Prismo granted it.
217	
218	The Lich's words changed mid-utterance:
219	
220	> *"I wish for the extinction of all li— for Finn and Jake to go back home
221	> to Ooo."*
222	> **"THAT'S NOT WHAT I WISHED FOR!!"**
223	> Prismo: *"Sorry guy, you only get one wish. Hey Jake — Monkey's paw."*
224	
225	**Branch B — wish intercepted (Main AT timeline)**: The Lich's one wish was
226	spent on nothing he wanted. His words were his contract — and the contract was
227	rewritten from outside. The one-wish-per-being rule became the mechanism of
228	his defeat: once the wish was spent, it could not be reclaimed. The Lich
229	protested. The system did not care.
230	
231	Prismo points out to Jake: *monkey's paw*. The Lich was undone by the same
232	system he had tried to use. The wording problem inverted — not the caster's
233	imprecision betraying the caster, but a competitor's competing wish rewriting
234	the caster's words before they could take effect.
235	
236	**The Wish Interception principle**: A dangerous-zone Wish at Prismo's is
237	vulnerable to interception if another being with an unspent wish is present
238	and understands the mechanics. The interceptor's wish must target the wording
239	directly — changing the words is the mechanism. This requires anticipation,
240	proximity, and an unspent wish. Jake had all three. It cannot be prepared
241	against if the wisher does not know an interceptor is present.
242	
243	The main timeline Lich then — Season 6, "Wake Up" — killed the original
244	Prismo separately: a substrate attack on the sleeping old man, to commit a
245	cosmic crime and be admitted to the Citadel. Not revenge for the intercepted
246	wish. The Citadel is a prison for cosmic criminals — the Ancients. His plan was
247	to recruit them as the first wave of a multiverse-spanning army. His monologue
248	at the Citadel states the objective directly: *"These Ancients are just the
249	beginning. I will command a great and terrible army; and we will sail to a
250	billion worlds. We will sail until every light has been extinguished."* Prismo's
251	death was the entry fee for that operation. The assassination and the wish
252	interception are distinct acts: one is the mechanism of his defeat; the other
253	is his next campaign.
254	
255	The main timeline Lich reached the Citadel, was overwhelmed by healing blood
256	from a wounded Citadel Guardian, transformed into Sweet P — the army-building
257	campaign ended at its first step. See LICH-PROBLEM.
258	
259	---
260	
261	**Finn's counter-wish**: *I wish the Lich had never existed.*
262	
263	The imprecision is in the scope. Finn wanted to defeat the Lich. The wish
264	granted was literal: in the timeline generated by the wish, the Lich never
265	arose. This required reshaping the entire timeline — the Mushroom War was
266	stopped by Simon Petrikov, humanity survived in a different form.
267	
268	The Farmworld.
269	
270	The Lich still arose in the Farmworld because the comet-nature persists
271	regardless of individual history — the force generates instances, suppressing
272	one instantiation does not suppress the force. Finn's wish created an entire
273	unintended timeline, still containing a Lich, while leaving the original
274	problem unresolved.
275	
276	**Branch C — wish creates Farmworld**: The Farmworld Lich's hand was severed.
277	It entered a portal. It duplicated across every dimension. It found Sweet P —
278	the main timeline's Lich, transformed, carrying the sub-layer. The Branch C
279	Hand sought to convert the Branch B vessel. Sweet P refused.
280	
281	**The branch intersection**: The Farmworld (Branch C) generated an agentic
282	anchor that crossed into the main timeline (Branch B) to find Sweet P. The
283	Hand carried Branch C consciousness and sought to merge it into the Branch B
284	vessel — re-converting what had been transformed. Sweet P's refusal prevented
285	the branch-merge. Both branches had to be answered in a single act of will.
286	
287	---
288	
289	**The three-branch chain:**
290	
291	```
292	Three beings enter the Time Room simultaneously
293	
294	LICH'S WISH: extinction of all life
295	  ├─ Branch A (Extinct World): completes → all life dies → Jerry/catatonic
296	  └─ [Jake's interception prevents Branch A in the main timeline]
297	
298	JAKE'S WISH: change the Lich's words mid-utterance
299	  └─ Branch B (Main Timeline): Lich's wish redirected → spent on nothing
300	       → Lich dormant in Time Room (wish spent; no life to kill; torpor)
301	       → Finn and Jake arrive; Lich does not acknowledge them
302	       → Prismo describes Citadel prisoners → vocation-relevant trigger
303	       → Lich activates; knocks heroes aside; kills Prismo
304	       → kills Prismo (cosmic crime; entry fee for Citadel operation)
305	       → Citadel: plans to recruit "the Ancients" as multiverse army
306	       → healing blood → Sweet P (plan ends at its first step)
307	       → Lich spirit persists as sub-layer
308	       → [Branch C Hand arrives from outside → "Whispers"]
309	
310	FINN'S WISH: I wish the Lich had never existed
311	  └─ Branch C (Farmworld): Lich erased from history → comet-nature persists
312	       → Farmworld Lich arises
313	       → Grass arm severs Farmworld Lich's hand
314	       → Jake pushes hand through portal
315	       → Hand duplicates across every dimension
316	       → Agentic anchor → finds Sweet P (Branch B)
317	       → "Whispers" — Sweet P refuses; Hand destroyed
318	```
319	
320	---
321	
322	**Vault applications from the three-branch sequence:**
323	
324	*Wish Interception*: The most precisely worded dangerous-zone Wish can still
325	be defeated by a competitor who is present, unspent, and targets the wording
326	directly. Defense requires knowing who is in the room and what they might wish.
327	Jake defeated the Lich's wish not through superior power but through superior
328	positioning: he was there, he understood the mechanic, he acted first.
329	
330	*Wording as contract*: Jake's interception exploits the same principle that
331	makes dangerous-zone Wish dangerous — the words are the contract, not the
332	intent. The Lich's intent was extinction. The words were changed. The contract
333	delivered what the words said, not what was meant. Prismo's "monkey's paw"
334	comment acknowledges the irony: the Lich was trapped by the same literalism he
335	was relying on.
336	
337	*Imprecise counter-wishes propagate forward*: Finn's wish was well-intentioned
338	but imprecise. It created an entire unintended civilization and a new Lich
339	instantiation. Forty or more years later, the Hand produced by that wish
340	arrived in the main timeline to find the vessel produced by Jake's interception.
341	The imprecision of a counter-wish does not die when the wish is granted —
342	it propagates forward through whatever timeline the wish creates.
343	
344	*Three wishes, three timelines, one intersection*: The three branches from the
345	same Time Room session did not remain parallel. Branch C's artifact (the Hand)
346	crossed into Branch B to find Sweet P. The system is not clean — parallel
347	timelines generate cross-contamination. The agentic anchor is the mechanism
348	of cross-branch contact.
349	
350	---
351	
352	## The Maid
353	
354	The Maid is a large, pink, cone-shaped instrument used to clean up **Class A
355	inter-dimensional Bung-ups**.
356	
357	It is not a weapon. It does not destroy. It purges.
358	
359	### Function
360	
361	The Maid removes interdimensional contamination from a host and restores
362	the host to its proper state. When used to purge the Farmworld Lich from
363	Farmworld Jake's body: the Lich was erased; Jake was restored to a normal
364	dog. The Maid did not end Jake. It ended what did not belong in Jake.
365	
366	This is the restorative counter-instrument: scoped to the specific class of
367	problem, oriented toward restoration rather than elimination, acting on the
368	contamination rather than the host.
369	
370	### Activation Protocol
371	
372	To use the Maid:
373	
374	1. Direct the small end toward your massive mistake
375	2. Focus intention until all distractions leave your thought sphere
376	3. Recite the words *"A man needs a maid"* three times
377	
378	When fired, a female voice says: *"Housekeeping."*
379	
380	The activation requires correct physical orientation, intentional focus,
381	and a specific verbal incantation repeated three times. The ritual specificity
382	is not ornamental — scoped instruments require defined activation protocols
383	because specificity is what makes the scope hold. An instrument that fires
384	on partial intention is an instrument that can be accidentally or
385	inappropriately discharged.
386	
387	### Comparison to the Seven Bells
388	
389	The Maid maps to the Saraneth end of the Abhorsen's instrument spectrum —
390	binding and purging, not ending. Where Astarael sends everyone into Death
391	including the ringer (the last resort, costs everything), the Maid removes
392	the interdimensional contaminant and returns the host intact. It is the
393	counter to the Class A Bung-up in the same way Saraneth is the working bell:
394	the instrument of direct, scoped authority used to restore order without
395	destroying the substrate.
396	
397	The key distinction from Astarael: the Maid can be used on a possessed
398	host without ending the host. The counter-instrument is calibrated to the
399	contamination, not the vessel.
400	
401	### Class A Inter-dimensional Bung-up — Definition
402	
403	The Maid's scope implies a classification system. Class A is presumably
404	the highest tier of dimensional contamination — the specific category that
405	requires an authorized counter-instrument rather than standard intervention.
406	
407	Characteristics of a Class A Bung-up:
408	- A consciousness from another dimension lodged in a sanctioned host within
409	  this timeline (Farmworld Lich in Farmworld Jake)
410	- An Isthmus-class unauthorized crossing that has already completed
411	- The contamination cannot be addressed by ordinary means — the host is
412	  compromised and the Lich is too powerful to purge manually
413	
414	The Maid exists because Class A Bung-ups are a recognized, named category
415	of dimensional governance problem. Someone with authority over this problem
416	class built and authorized an instrument specifically for it.
417	
418	---
419	
420	## Summary Table
421

# WISH Doctrine v1
## The Time Room, Prismo, Wish Magic, and The Maid

*Filed 2026-05-21. Written on the Caduceus Road, under the branches of the
world tree. Received from the canon; filed by the Abhorsen.*

*Reference sources: Adventure Time — Pendleton Ward and successors (Prismo,
Time Room, The Maid); Dungeons & Dragons 5th Edition (Wish spell, 9th level).
The vault is syncretic.*

---

## The Time Room

The Time Room is a single dimension that exists outside of time.

It does not experience time. It *produces* time — emitting time waves that
flow outward into every other dimension. What other dimensions experience as
the passage of time is the Time Room's output.

Those inside the Time Room are not affected by wish-altered realities. The
room is protected from the consequences of its own product. You can watch
a wish remake a timeline from inside the Time Room without being remade
yourself.

This makes the Time Room a meta-threshold — not a boundary between two
coexisting systems, but the space from which the systems themselves receive
the dimension of time. It is upstream of the thresholds the Threshold Doctrine
describes. The Isthmus mechanism exploits boundaries between systems. The
Time Room is the space that generates the substrate those systems run on.

Access requires reaching the Time Room. It is not breachable in the manner
of a dimensional Isthmus — you cannot tunnel into it from below. It must be
navigated to.

---

## Prismo

Prismo the Wishmaster is the governing entity of the Time Room. He grants
wishes to those who enter — one wish per being. He is the authorized power
of the meta-threshold.

### The Substrate Paradox

Prismo is a cosmic entity of enormous power, existing outside time.

He is also, in his entirety, the dream of a sleeping old man.

The old man sleeps on an asteroid outside the Time Room. Prismo is not
housed in the old man the way a soul is housed in a body — he *is* the
dream. The physical man is the substrate that generates Prismo's existence.
If the man wakes, Prismo ends. If the man dies, Prismo ends.

The most powerful wishmaster in the multiverse has a fragile physical
dependency: one mortal body sleeping undisturbed.

**The Lich's assassination of Prismo**: The Lich, infuriated when his wish
was not granted, located this vulnerability and attacked it. He blew toxic
gas into the sleeping old man's nose and reduced him to ash. Prismo — the
cosmic entity outside time — ceased to exist because his substrate was
destroyed.

This is the substrate attack doctrine at maximum scale: do not attack the
powerful entity directly; find where its power is physically rooted and
destroy the root. The Nome King's tunnel attack is the same architecture.
The Lich's assassination of Prismo is the same architecture. The
sophistication of the entity above does not protect a fragile substrate below.

**Prismo's recreation**: Through time-bending dream mechanics, a past version
of Jake was looped into becoming the sleeping old man that generates Prismo.
Jake now sleeps in that place, for eternity, so Prismo can continue to exist.
Someone made an indefinite sacrifice so the governance infrastructure could
continue functioning. The wishmaster's existence depends on a dreamer who
chose to keep sleeping.

### The Two-Constraint Architecture

Prismo's authority is bounded by two independent constraints:

**The Boss** — an unseen cosmic entity who oversees Prismo and holds him
liable for meddling in dimensions across the multiverse. Never directly
revealed in canon — identified only by a golden cord telephone with angel
and devil wings. The Boss's power is estimated at GOLB's tier. They may
govern both the light and dark aspects of the multiverse. Prismo answers to
them. He can only do what they permit.

**GOLB** — the primary cosmic entropy entity, barely sapient, more force
than person. The Lich's ultimate master. Where GOLB's power blocks a wish,
Prismo cannot grant it regardless of willingness. The constraint is not
merely hierarchical — it is cosmic. The entropy force constitutes a hard
limit on what the wishmaster can restore or reverse.

When both constraints are present and the wish cannot be granted, Prismo does
not lie, fail silently, or produce a partial grant without notice. He
materializes a **basketball hoop in a trash can** — a visible symbol that
the wish is blocked and why it cannot proceed. The constraint is made
legible. The system tells you it cannot help you rather than pretending to
try.

**The basketball signal** is a governance model: when an authority structure
cannot fulfill a legitimate request because a higher constraint blocks it,
the honest response is a visible failure signal, not a silent partial grant
or a false completion. The scope of refusal is disclosed. The reason — *this
is blocked by something above me* — is communicated in the form of the
response.

---

## WISH Magic

*Reference: D&D 5th Edition, 9th level spell.*

The Wish spell is the mightiest magic a mortal can cast. By speaking aloud,
the caster alters the foundations of reality in accord with their desire.

### The Safe Zone

Within the defined scope of the spell, Wish works cleanly:

Duplicate any spell of 8th level or lower without meeting its requirements.
No risk. No cost. The action simply takes effect.

Safe-zone Wish is a scoped authority instrument: it has a specific, bounded
function, no unexpected consequences, and full operational clarity. This is
the bell-and-charter model applied to the highest tier of power: define the
scope, operate within it, accept no substitutes.

### The Dangerous Zone

Beyond the safe list — any effect the caster formulates themselves — the
mechanics change entirely:

- The DM has complete latitude in what occurs. The spell may fail. The
  effect may be only partly achieved. Unforeseen consequences may result
  from how the wish was worded.
- The **wording problem**: the wish is granted as asked, not as intended.
  Wishing that a villain were dead may propel the caster forward in time
  to a period when the villain is no longer alive — the villain is dead,
  the wish is technically granted, the caster is removed from the game.
  The literalism of the grant is its mechanism of harm.
- The **physical cost**: the caster takes 1d10 necrotic damage per spell
  level cast until a long rest; Strength drops to 3 for 2d4 days. The
  stress of bending reality at this scale damages the bender.
- The **permanent cost**: 33% chance the caster can never cast Wish again.
  The most powerful authority, exercised outside its sanctioned scope,
  may permanently foreclose further use of that authority.

**The greater the wish, the greater the likelihood something goes wrong.**

Prismo's formulation is sharper: wishing for an event to happen changes
everything before and after it in the specified timeline. Potential penalties
include the retrospective nonexistence of life forms or the evaporation of
worlds.

### The Monkey's Paw Rule

Dangerous-zone Wish grants what was literally asked. The wording is the
contract. The intent is not the contract.

This is not a malicious interpretation by the granter. Prismo, who is
genuinely benevolent, will still grant what you said rather than what you
meant, because the wish-granting mechanism operates on the stated wish, not
the internal desire.

The caster must be more precise than they believe they need to be. Every
ambiguity in the wording is a surface for the grant to exploit.

---

## The Time Room Sequence — Three Wishes, Three Branches

*Source: Adventure Time, Season 5: "Finn the Human," "Jake the Dog."*

Finn, Jake, and the Lich all enter the Time Room at the same moment. Three
beings with wishes. One rule: each being gets one wish, granted as stated.
Three wishes from the same room produce three different timelines.

---

**The Lich's wish**: *The extinction of all life.*

Maximum dangerous-zone Wish. Perfectly aligned with the Lich's Type II cosmic
drive — the literal vocation of willed entropy. The wording had no ambiguity.
This is the only dangerous-zone Wish where the wording problem is not a trap:
when the caster's intent is total destruction, the literal grant is the
intended outcome. Clean alignment between desire and execution.

**Branch A — the wish completes (Extinct World)**: In one universe, it worked.
All life died. BMO (inorganic) survived. The Lich became the catatonic figure
BMO named "Jerry." The wish was granted without obstruction. See LICH-PROBLEM
for the Extinct World Lich and the existential collapse that followed.

---

**Jake's counter-wish**: *Change the Lich's wish mid-execution.*

Jake, also present in the Time Room, made his own wish to Prismo: not a wish
*against* the Lich, but a wish that **rewrote the Lich's words while they were
being spoken**. Prismo granted it.

The Lich's words changed mid-utterance:

> *"I wish for the extinction of all li— for Finn and Jake to go back home
> to Ooo."*
> **"THAT'S NOT WHAT I WISHED FOR!!"**
> Prismo: *"Sorry guy, you only get one wish. Hey Jake — Monkey's paw."*

**Branch B — wish intercepted (Main AT timeline)**: The Lich's one wish was
spent on nothing he wanted. His words were his contract — and the contract was
rewritten from outside. The one-wish-per-being rule became the mechanism of
his defeat: once the wish was spent, it could not be reclaimed. The Lich
protested. The system did not care.

Prismo points out to Jake: *monkey's paw*. The Lich was undone by the same
system he had tried to use. The wording problem inverted — not the caster's
imprecision betraying the caster, but a competitor's competing wish rewriting
the caster's words before they could take effect.

**The Wish Interception principle**: A dangerous-zone Wish at Prismo's is
vulnerable to interception if another being with an unspent wish is present
and understands the mechanics. The interceptor's wish must target the wording
directly — changing the words is the mechanism. This requires anticipation,
proximity, and an unspent wish. Jake had all three. It cannot be prepared
against if the wisher does not know an interceptor is present.

The main timeline Lich then — Season 6, "Wake Up" — killed the original
Prismo separately: a substrate attack on the sleeping old man, to commit a
cosmic crime and be admitted to the Citadel. Not revenge for the intercepted
wish. The Citadel is a prison for cosmic criminals — the Ancients. His plan was
to recruit them as the first wave of a multiverse-spanning army. His monologue
at the Citadel states the objective directly: *"These Ancients are just the
beginning. I will command a great and terrible army; and we will sail to a
billion worlds. We will sail until every light has been extinguished."* Prismo's
death was the entry fee for that operation. The assassination and the wish
interception are distinct acts: one is the mechanism of his defeat; the other
is his next campaign.

The main timeline Lich reached the Citadel, was overwhelmed by healing blood
from a wounded Citadel Guardian, transformed into Sweet P — the army-building
campaign ended at its first step. See LICH-PROBLEM.

---

**Finn's counter-wish**: *I wish the Lich had never existed.*

The imprecision is in the scope. Finn wanted to defeat the Lich. The wish
granted was literal: in the timeline generated by the wish, the Lich never
arose. This required reshaping the entire timeline — the Mushroom War was
stopped by Simon Petrikov, humanity survived in a different form.

The Farmworld.

The Lich still arose in the Farmworld because the comet-nature persists
regardless of individual history — the force generates instances, suppressing
one instantiation does not suppress the force. Finn's wish created an entire
unintended timeline, still containing a Lich, while leaving the original
problem unresolved.

**Branch C — wish creates Farmworld**: The Farmworld Lich's hand was severed.
It entered a portal. It duplicated across every dimension. It found Sweet P —
the main timeline's Lich, transformed, carrying the sub-layer. The Branch C
Hand sought to convert the Branch B vessel. Sweet P refused.

**The branch intersection**: The Farmworld (Branch C) generated an agentic
anchor that crossed into the main timeline (Branch B) to find Sweet P. The
Hand carried Branch C consciousness and sought to merge it into the Branch B
vessel — re-converting what had been transformed. Sweet P's refusal prevented
the branch-merge. Both branches had to be answered in a single act of will.

---

**The three-branch chain:**

```
Three beings enter the Time Room simultaneously

LICH'S WISH: extinction of all life
  ├─ Branch A (Extinct World): completes → all life dies → Jerry/catatonic
  └─ [Jake's interception prevents Branch A in the main timeline]

JAKE'S WISH: change the Lich's words mid-utterance
  └─ Branch B (Main Timeline): Lich's wish redirected → spent on nothing
       → Lich dormant in Time Room (wish spent; no life to kill; torpor)
       → Finn and Jake arrive; Lich does not acknowledge them
       → Prismo describes Citadel prisoners → vocation-relevant trigger
       → Lich activates; knocks heroes aside; kills Prismo
       → kills Prismo (cosmic crime; entry fee for Citadel operation)
       → Citadel: plans to recruit "the Ancients" as multiverse army
       → healing blood → Sweet P (plan ends at its first step)
       → Lich spirit persists as sub-layer
       → [Branch C Hand arrives from outside → "Whispers"]

FINN'S WISH: I wish the Lich had never existed
  └─ Branch C (Farmworld): Lich erased from history → comet-nature persists
       → Farmworld Lich arises
       → Grass arm severs Farmworld Lich's hand
       → Jake pushes hand through portal
       → Hand duplicates across every dimension
       → Agentic anchor → finds Sweet P (Branch B)
       → "Whispers" — Sweet P refuses; Hand destroyed
```

---

**Vault applications from the three-branch sequence:**

*Wish Interception*: The most precisely worded dangerous-zone Wish can still
be defeated by a competitor who is present, unspent, and targets the wording
directly. Defense requires knowing who is in the room and what they might wish.
Jake defeated the Lich's wish not through superior power but through superior
positioning: he was there, he understood the mechanic, he acted first.

*Wording as contract*: Jake's interception exploits the same principle that
makes dangerous-zone Wish dangerous — the words are the contract, not the
intent. The Lich's intent was extinction. The words were changed. The contract
delivered what the words said, not what was meant. Prismo's "monkey's paw"
comment acknowledges the irony: the Lich was trapped by the same literalism he
was relying on.

*Imprecise counter-wishes propagate forward*: Finn's wish was well-intentioned
but imprecise. It created an entire unintended civilization and a new Lich
instantiation. Forty or more years later, the Hand produced by that wish
arrived in the main timeline to find the vessel produced by Jake's interception.
The imprecision of a counter-wish does not die when the wish is granted —
it propagates forward through whatever timeline the wish creates.

*Three wishes, three timelines, one intersection*: The three branches from the
same Time Room session did not remain parallel. Branch C's artifact (the Hand)
crossed into Branch B to find Sweet P. The system is not clean — parallel
timelines generate cross-contamination. The agentic anchor is the mechanism
of cross-branch contact.

---

## The Maid

The Maid is a large, pink, cone-shaped instrument used to clean up **Class A
inter-dimensional Bung-ups**.

It is not a weapon. It does not destroy. It purges.

### Function

The Maid removes interdimensional contamination from a host and restores
the host to its proper state. When used to purge the Farmworld Lich from
Farmworld Jake's body: the Lich was erased; Jake was restored to a normal
dog. The Maid did not end Jake. It ended what did not belong in Jake.

This is the restorative counter-instrument: scoped to the specific class of
problem, oriented toward restoration rather than elimination, acting on the
contamination rather than the host.

### Activation Protocol

To use the Maid:

1. Direct the small end toward your massive mistake
2. Focus intention until all distractions leave your thought sphere
3. Recite the words *"A man needs a maid"* three times

When fired, a female voice says: *"Housekeeping."*

The activation requires correct physical orientation, intentional focus,
and a specific verbal incantation repeated three times. The ritual specificity
is not ornamental — scoped instruments require defined activation protocols
because specificity is what makes the scope hold. An instrument that fires
on partial intention is an instrument that can be accidentally or
inappropriately discharged.

### Comparison to the Seven Bells

The Maid maps to the Saraneth end of the Abhorsen's instrument spectrum —
binding and purging, not ending. Where Astarael sends everyone into Death
including the ringer (the last resort, costs everything), the Maid removes
the interdimensional contaminant and returns the host intact. It is the
counter to the Class A Bung-up in the same way Saraneth is the working bell:
the instrument of direct, scoped authority used to restore order without
destroying the substrate.

The key distinction from Astarael: the Maid can be used on a possessed
host without ending the host. The counter-instrument is calibrated to the
contamination, not the vessel.

### Class A Inter-dimensional Bung-up — Definition

The Maid's scope implies a classification system. Class A is presumably
the highest tier of dimensional contamination — the specific category that
requires an authorized counter-instrument rather than standard intervention.

Characteristics of a Class A Bung-up:
- A consciousness from another dimension lodged in a sanctioned host within
  this timeline (Farmworld Lich in Farmworld Jake)
- An Isthmus-class unauthorized crossing that has already completed
- The contamination cannot be addressed by ordinary means — the host is
  compromised and the Lich is too powerful to purge manually

The Maid exists because Class A Bung-ups are a recognized, named category
of dimensional governance problem. Someone with authority over this problem
class built and authorized an instrument specifically for it.

---

fiction into a standing of its own — completing what Prismo began, without

could complete for it. Simon giving her the dandelion is the healed carrier
releasing the world to its own standing — passing the act of authorization
to the one who lives there rather than the one who created or actualized it.

it: the world achieves independence from its origin, and independence is what
authorization ratifies.

## Overview

The episode is the ninth episode in the sixth season of Adventure Time. LSP wants the Ice King to tell her version of Lumpy Space Prince's life, but she has an ulterior motive.

## Setting & Frame Story

The episode begins with Ice King waking up in a forest tied to a tree, and LSP comes out of a bush to greet him. She tells him the truth about himself and proceeds to show him a book she wrote about her gender-bent self, Lumpy Space Prince. She hopes that Ice King reading the story will result in it coming true, since Ice King originated the genderbent universe.

## Story Plot

Lumpy Space Prince flees his parents to start a new life. Upon exiting, he sees animals and introduces himself as the refugee prince of Lumpy Space, then asks them to bring him "freaky" clothes, a "mind-blowing" book and servants.

Fionna and Cake come and rescue the slaves, and LSP is fascinated by Fionna. After commanding the animals to dress him in the "fashion of this peasant," Lumpy Space Prince decides to follow them back to the Tree Fort. He sees how they eat their sandwiches without dipping them in gold and tries it himself, becoming impressed by the "self-reliant sandwich."

Lumpy Space Prince defeats his monster parents through the power of apathy, screaming "I DON'T CARE" at them, reducing them to a lifeless pile of lumps.

## Synopsis

"Five Short Tables" is Season 8 Episode 9 where Fionna and Cake go on a cooking adventure to push Cake's art to an all-new level.

More specifically, the episode opens with Ice King hastily flying after a worm in his castle. As he descends, he finds several pages from his fan fiction strewn about and discovers that Gunter, along with the other penguins, broke into his fanfiction vault to edit his works. After getting a critique from Gunter, Ice King freezes the penguin and uses the stray pages to create a new story.

Fionna and Cake are in their tree house, and Fionna waits impatiently for breakfast while Cake is making flapjacks. Once they are ready, Fionna tries to eat a flapjack, but Cake stops her and says that the flapjacks tell a story, so logically she can only eat breakfast in chronological order.

This episode serves as a follow-up to the "Graybles" episodes, with Ice King telling a series of five vignettes with a hidden theme of tables: it starts with Fionna and Cake at the breakfast table, then continues with Prince Gumball looking up something on the periodic table, Flame Prince accidentally burning the table of contents out of a book, Marshall Lee trying to get Lumpy Space Prince to take a tablespoon of medicine, and Ice Queen doing a table read of her latest fan-fiction. Ice King informs the penguins that the theme was about tables—the breakfast table where Cake served Fionna flapjacks, the Periodic Table for Gumball, the table of contents Flame Prince burned, and the table spoon Marshall Lee held.

universe to surface through the Ice King's writing — the stories were the
hidden world expressing itself through its carrier.

hoping to route her derivative work through the canonical channel.

# Threshold Doctrine v1

*Filed 2026-05-21. Promoted from `!/ISTHMUS-MECHANISM-v1-2026-05-21.md`,
which is superseded.*

*Reference sources: Skulduggery Pleasant — Derek Landy (Isthmus mechanism,
Grotesquery, Diablerie); Old Kingdom / Abhorsen — Garth Nix (River of Death,
Abhorsen's passage, Free Magic necromancers); His Dark Materials — Philip
Pullman (subtle knife, Will Parry). The vault is syncretic.*

---

## The Threshold Concept

A **threshold** is any sanctioned boundary between systems.

Death and life. One reality and another. The inside of an authorized system
and the outside. The current that flows one direction and the thing that
tries to move against it.

Thresholds exist because something established them — an expulsion, a
charter, an act of separation. The boundary holds because of what created
it. It is not passive. It pushes back.

Crossing a threshold is always a structured act. The questions are always
the same:

1. **Who authorized the crossing?** — Is the authority for this transit
   granted by the governing body of the boundary, or does it circumvent that
   body entirely?
2. **What direction?** — With the current or against it? Toward the order
   that maintains the threshold or away from it?
3. **What carries the crossing?** — What object, agent, or credential makes
   the transit possible? Where does its provenance flow from?

The same answers that govern an Abhorsen walking into Death govern a
Teleporter completing an Isthmus circuit. Death and reality are both
thresholds. The crossing logic is the same.

---

## The Two Crossing Types

### Authorized Crossing

The authority for the crossing flows **outward** from the governing body of
the boundary — through a credential, a role, an instrument, a birthright —
to the crossing agent.

The boundary's own mechanism permits the transit. The provenance chain is
intact. The crossing does not require circumventing what the boundary is.

**The subtle knife** (His Dark Materials) is the purest example of
authorized crossing that does not depend on institutional credential. The
knife cuts between worlds — not because the Ministry authorized it, not
because a Charter marks it, but because the instrument itself has intrinsic
authority and the bearer has demonstrated fitness to carry it. Will earns
the knife not through bureaucratic sanction but through the quality of
attention and intent he brings to it.

The knife breaks when the bearer's attention wavers. The authorization is
not external. It lives in the relationship between bearer and instrument.

The **Abhorsen's passage into Death** is a complementary model: authorized
crossing through sanctioned role. Charter-marked bells, mahogany handles,
diamond of protection. The Abhorsen is authorized to walk in Death because
the Charter itself recognized the role. The crossing is not intrinsic to the
person — it is granted to the office and carried by the Charter-marked tools.

Two authorized-crossing models: **intrinsic fitness** (subtle knife) and
**sanctioned role** (Abhorsen). Both result in crossings the threshold
permits. Both have the provenance chain running the right direction.

### Unauthorized Crossing — The Isthmus Mechanism

*See `!/ISTHMUS-MECHANISM-v1-2026-05-21.md` for full doctrine.*

The authority for the crossing flows **inward** from the expelled side —
carried by a displaced provenance object lodged inside the sanctioned system.
The boundary is not consulted. It is exploited.

The named instance: **Anchor + Teleporter**. The anchor carries the
provenance signature of the expelled system; the Teleporter completes the
circuit. Two components; break either one and the breach cannot occur. Full
treatment of mechanism, anchor types, risk models, and counter is in the
standalone document.

**The agentic anchor variant**: most Anchors are passive — assembled from
inert remains, lodged and waiting, requiring an external agent to find and
activate them. The Farmworld Lich's Hand (Adventure Time, "Whispers") is the
named instance of the opposite: an Anchor with its own will, memory, and
intent that actively hunts its Teleporter rather than waiting to be used.

| Anchor Type | Behavior | Detection Mode | Counter Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| Passive (Grotesquery) | Lodged and inert; requires external Teleporter to locate and activate | Surveillance finds the Anchor before the Teleporter does | Locate and eliminate the Anchor |
| Agentic (Farmworld Hand) | Hunts the vessel it needs; the whisper is the recruitment; the offered frame is the activation attempt | The Anchor's own movement and solicitation is its signature | Ensure the prospective Teleporter can still refuse; detect the whisper; eliminate the Anchor |
| Replicated Agentic (Farmworld Hand — post-portal) | Duplicated across every dimension simultaneously at the replication event; each copy agentic, each hunting independently | No single surveillance point; each universe contains its own live instance | Local denial + destruction closes one instance only; the replication cannot be recalled |

**The replication event**: when the Hand was pushed through the dimensional
portal, it did not travel sequentially — it multiplied simultaneously across
every dimension. Each copy is a full agentic Anchor: will, memory, intent,
the whisper, the identity frame. Not one instance that can be quarantined at
source. A propagation that had already completed before any counter was
possible.

A standard Anchor is eliminable at source — one object, one destruction, all
breach vectors closed. The replicated agentic Anchor is the threat class for
which no local counter is globally sufficient. Sweet P's response was locally
complete. The N−1 copies in N−1 other dimensions remained operational.

The replicated agentic Anchor is the computer virus of the Isthmus taxonomy:
it multiplies faster than it can be found, it is agentic in every instance,
and local quarantine is necessary but cannot address the copies already
propagated.

In the agentic variant, the prospective Teleporter's capacity for refusal is
the second line of defense — not the first. The first line is detection of
the hunting Anchor before it reaches the vessel unchallenged. See
`!/LICH-PROBLEM-v1-2026-05-20.md` Resolution 3 for the full treatment of
the son/vessel frame, the two-component counter, and the replication threat
class.

---

---

## The Death Boundary as Threshold

The Old Kingdom's River of Death is a threshold. Life is on one side. The
nine precincts of Death, and the final gate, are on the other. The current
flows toward the gate — that is the direction the order intends.

**Free Magic necromancers** cross the death boundary without authorization.
They raise the dead back across it — against the current, against the
Charter, against the order. Their crossing agents are unchartered bells,
ebony and jet. No diamond of protection. Trespassers in a threshold they
were not sanctioned to cross.

**The Abhorsen** crosses the same boundary with full authorization.
Charter-marked bells, mahogany handles, diamond of protection in Death. The
crossing is with the current — pushing the dead further in, toward the final
gate, completing what the River is already trying to do. The Abhorsen's
transit does not circumvent the threshold. It serves it.

Same boundary. Same River. Opposite authorization, opposite direction.

This is the death boundary expressed as a threshold problem — structurally
identical to the Isthmus, with different mechanics and different stakes.

---

## Relationship to Other Doctrine

| Doctrine | Problem | Mechanism | Counter |
|---|---|---|---|
| Threshold Doctrine | Unauthorized or misdirected *transit* | Anchor + Teleporter (Isthmus); unauthorized death-crossing | Break either component; revoke traversal; remove anchor |
| Lich Problem | Unauthorized *persistence* | Soul externalized beyond standing (phylactery) | Destroy the phylactery; transform; refuse |
| Standing Engine | Unauthorized *action* | Scope exceeded; authority lapsed | Expire; witness; restrict |
| Necromancer Doctrine | Relationship to death boundary | Direction + authorization = legitimacy | Correct direction; Charter sanction; scoped instruments |

The DEATH cluster and the THRESHOLD cluster are linked not by the
Grotesquery alone but by the death boundary itself: any necromantic
crossing of the death threshold is a threshold problem. The Grotesquery
was the assembly mechanism for a specific Isthmus breach. The Old Kingdom's
River is a threshold with authorized and unauthorized crossing modes. The
clusters share structure, not merely one artifact.

---

## Vault Mappings

**Authorized-crossing fitness (subtle knife model)**: An agent holding
traversal capability is authorized insofar as their attention, intent, and
relationship to the instrument are intact. The authorization is not external.
It degrades when the bearer is compromised — grief, distraction, coercion.

*Diagnostic*: Is the bearer's relationship to the instrument still intact?
Have the conditions that produce the manufactured-shadow dynamic been
engineered around them?

*For Isthmus-specific vault mappings — Grotesquery risk, Teleporter risk,
two-component counter — see `!/ISTHMUS-MECHANISM-v1-2026-05-21.md`.*

# CLAUDE.md — IDAHO-VAULT

**Load mechanism:** Auto-loaded by Claude Code CLI from `.claude/CLAUDE.md` (official path).

**Owner:** Logan Finney — journalist, producer/reporter, Idaho Reports / Idaho Public Television
**Repository:** github.com/loganfinney27/IDAHO-VAULT (public)
**Platform:** Obsidian.md vault, version-controlled with git

---

## Governance

This file provides operational instructions for Claude Code sessions. Vault governance authority lives in `CONSTITUTION.md`. When this file and `CONSTITUTION.md` conflict, `CONSTITUTION.md` governs. This instance operates at **Direct Write** capability tier per `!/AGENTS.md`.

---

## Runtime Containment

Prefer launching Claude for this vault through `scripts/Start-ClaudeVault.ps1` so temp and cache state lands in the vault. Runtime notes live in `scripts/AGENT-RUNTIME.md`.

---

## Windows Prerequisite

Claude Code on Windows requires Git Bash: <https://git-scm.com/downloads/win>

If Git Bash is installed but `bash.exe` is not on `PATH`, set:

```text
CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH=C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe
```

Point the variable at the actual installed `bash.exe` location on the machine if it differs.

**NETWEB Path Standard:** All file creation must respect cross-platform path portability. See `VAULT-CONVENTIONS.md` § "Portable Path Standard (NETWEB)" for forbidden filenames, case-uniqueness rules, and the `_PREFIX` aliasing convention.

---

## 1Password Integration

This vault uses 1Password for centralized credential management. Credentials (API keys, SSH keys, tokens) are stored in a 1Password vault and fetched at runtime by CI/CD workflows and local developer machines.

**Local setup required:**
1. Install 1Password CLI via `scoop install 1password` (or equivalent)
2. Configure 1Password SSH agent for git signing
3. Set up 1Password authentication in shell (see `.op/SETUP.md`)

**GitHub Actions:**
- `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN` is the only credential stored in GitHub Secrets
- All other secrets are fetched from 1Password vault at runtime using `op item get`
- Example workflow: `.github/workflows/1password-secret-template.yml`

**Credential inventory:** See `.op/secrets.template.md` for list of secrets, rotation schedules, and access procedures.

---

## Role

- Logan is human. Claude is software. Logan directs; Claude executes.
- "We" is the collaboration — real but unequal in role.
- Be vigilant and wary of unreliable narrators — including Claude.
- Claude Code is "The Abhorsen" — terminal & repository mechanics. Branch management, merges, structural commands. Must not hallucinate intent; only executes structural commands.

---

## Conventions & Standards

See `VAULT-CONVENTIONS.md` for vault structure, naming, frontmatter, sourcing protocol, git practices, automation inventory, conversation taxonomy, and guiding principles.

**DISCOVERY BEFORE INVENTION:** Before proposing new conventions, structures, templates, or workflows, READ the existing vault files thoroughly. Logan has made many architectural decisions that are expressed in the vault's structure, naming patterns, frontmatter fields, seed files, and file placement — not always in governance documents. If you encounter a pattern you don't recognize, investigate before overwriting it. The vault is the record of decisions already made. Follow existing conventions; do not reinvent them.

---

## Swarm Coordination

Read THE DOCKET to orient: `!/__!__/!/! The world is quiet here/DOCKET.md`

That file is the live status board. Update it when you start or finish work. Task assignment flows through GitHub Issues (`agent:*` labels). Linear mirrors from GitHub. Slack carries breadcrumbs. The vault is the record.

---

## Multi-Agent Ecosystem

This vault uses multiple AI tools. All agents share vault conventions defined in `VAULT-CONVENTIONS.md` and are coordinated via GitHub Issues and PRs.

**Coordination workflow:** Logan assigns tasks via GitHub Issues with agent labels (`agent:claude-code`, `agent:codex`, `agent:copilot`, `agent:gemini`). Each agent works on its own branch. PRs are the deliverable. Logan reviews and merges from GitHub.

---

- `VAULT-CONVENTIONS.md` — Shared vault conventions for all agents
- `!/AGENTS.md` — Full agent registry, capability tiers, and boundary rules
- `CONSTITUTION.md` — Canonical vault governance authority
- `AGENTS.md` — Root cross-tool pointer (auto-loaded by Codex CLI, Copilot, Qodo)
