17	# WISH Doctrine v1
18	## The Time Room, Prismo, Wish Magic, and The Maid
19	
20	*Filed 2026-05-21. Written on the Caduceus Road, under the branches of the
21	world tree. Received from the canon; filed by the Abhorsen.*
22	
23	*Reference sources: Adventure Time — Pendleton Ward and successors (Prismo,
24	Time Room, The Maid); Dungeons & Dragons 5th Edition (Wish spell, 9th level).
25	The vault is syncretic.*
26	
27	---
28	
29	## The Time Room
30	
31	The Time Room is a single dimension that exists outside of time.
32	
33	It does not experience time. It *produces* time — emitting time waves that
34	flow outward into every other dimension. What other dimensions experience as
35	the passage of time is the Time Room's output.
36	
37	Those inside the Time Room are not affected by wish-altered realities. The
38	room is protected from the consequences of its own product. You can watch
39	a wish remake a timeline from inside the Time Room without being remade
40	yourself.
41	
42	This makes the Time Room a meta-threshold — not a boundary between two
43	coexisting systems, but the space from which the systems themselves receive
44	the dimension of time. It is upstream of the thresholds the Threshold Doctrine
45	describes. The Isthmus mechanism exploits boundaries between systems. The
46	Time Room is the space that generates the substrate those systems run on.
47	
48	Access requires reaching the Time Room. It is not breachable in the manner
49	of a dimensional Isthmus — you cannot tunnel into it from below. It must be
50	navigated to.
51	
52	---
53	
54	## Prismo
55	
56	Prismo the Wishmaster is the governing entity of the Time Room. He grants
57	wishes to those who enter — one wish per being. He is the authorized power
58	of the meta-threshold.
59	
60	### The Substrate Paradox
61	
62	Prismo is a cosmic entity of enormous power, existing outside time.
63	
64	He is also, in his entirety, the dream of a sleeping old man.
65	
66	The old man sleeps on an asteroid outside the Time Room. Prismo is not
67	housed in the old man the way a soul is housed in a body — he *is* the
68	dream. The physical man is the substrate that generates Prismo's existence.
69	If the man wakes, Prismo ends. If the man dies, Prismo ends.
70	
71	The most powerful wishmaster in the multiverse has a fragile physical
72	dependency: one mortal body sleeping undisturbed.
73	
74	**The Lich's assassination of Prismo**: The Lich, infuriated when his wish
75	was not granted, located this vulnerability and attacked it. He blew toxic
76	gas into the sleeping old man's nose and reduced him to ash. Prismo — the
77	cosmic entity outside time — ceased to exist because his substrate was
78	destroyed.
79	
80	This is the substrate attack doctrine at maximum scale: do not attack the
81	powerful entity directly; find where its power is physically rooted and
82	destroy the root. The Nome King's tunnel attack is the same architecture.
83	The Lich's assassination of Prismo is the same architecture. The
84	sophistication of the entity above does not protect a fragile substrate below.
85	
86	**Prismo's recreation**: Through time-bending dream mechanics, a past version
87	of Jake was looped into becoming the sleeping old man that generates Prismo.
88	Jake now sleeps in that place, for eternity, so Prismo can continue to exist.
89	Someone made an indefinite sacrifice so the governance infrastructure could
90	continue functioning. The wishmaster's existence depends on a dreamer who
91	chose to keep sleeping.
92	
93	### The Two-Constraint Architecture
94	
95	Prismo's authority is bounded by two independent constraints:
96	
97	**The Boss** — an unseen cosmic entity who oversees Prismo and holds him
98	liable for meddling in dimensions across the multiverse. Never directly
99	revealed in canon — identified only by a golden cord telephone with angel
100	and devil wings. The Boss's power is estimated at GOLB's tier. They may
101	govern both the light and dark aspects of the multiverse. Prismo answers to
102	them. He can only do what they permit.
103	
104	**GOLB** — the primary cosmic entropy entity, barely sapient, more force
105	than person. The Lich's ultimate master. Where GOLB's power blocks a wish,
106	Prismo cannot grant it regardless of willingness. The constraint is not
107	merely hierarchical — it is cosmic. The entropy force constitutes a hard
108	limit on what the wishmaster can restore or reverse.
109	
110	When both constraints are present and the wish cannot be granted, Prismo does
111	not lie, fail silently, or produce a partial grant without notice. He
112	materializes a **basketball hoop in a trash can** — a visible symbol that
113	the wish is blocked and why it cannot proceed. The constraint is made
114	legible. The system tells you it cannot help you rather than pretending to
115	try.
116	
117	**The basketball signal** is a governance model: when an authority structure
118	cannot fulfill a legitimate request because a higher constraint blocks it,
119	the honest response is a visible failure signal, not a silent partial grant
120	or a false completion. The scope of refusal is disclosed. The reason — *this
121	is blocked by something above me* — is communicated in the form of the
122	response.
123	
124	---
125	
126	## WISH Magic
127	
128	*Reference: D&D 5th Edition, 9th level spell.*
129	
130	The Wish spell is the mightiest magic a mortal can cast. By speaking aloud,
131	the caster alters the foundations of reality in accord with their desire.
132	
133	### The Safe Zone
134	
135	Within the defined scope of the spell, Wish works cleanly:
136	
137	Duplicate any spell of 8th level or lower without meeting its requirements.
138	No risk. No cost. The action simply takes effect.
139	
140	Safe-zone Wish is a scoped authority instrument: it has a specific, bounded
141	function, no unexpected consequences, and full operational clarity. This is
142	the bell-and-charter model applied to the highest tier of power: define the
143	scope, operate within it, accept no substitutes.
144	
145	### The Dangerous Zone
146	
147	Beyond the safe list — any effect the caster formulates themselves — the
148	mechanics change entirely:
149	
150	- The DM has complete latitude in what occurs. The spell may fail. The
151	  effect may be only partly achieved. Unforeseen consequences may result
152	  from how the wish was worded.
153	- The **wording problem**: the wish is granted as asked, not as intended.
154	  Wishing that a villain were dead may propel the caster forward in time
155	  to a period when the villain is no longer alive — the villain is dead,
156	  the wish is technically granted, the caster is removed from the game.
157	  The literalism of the grant is its mechanism of harm.
158	- The **physical cost**: the caster takes 1d10 necrotic damage per spell
159	  level cast until a long rest; Strength drops to 3 for 2d4 days. The
160	  stress of bending reality at this scale damages the bender.
161	- The **permanent cost**: 33% chance the caster can never cast Wish again.
162	  The most powerful authority, exercised outside its sanctioned scope,
163	  may permanently foreclose further use of that authority.
164	
165	**The greater the wish, the greater the likelihood something goes wrong.**
166	
167	Prismo's formulation is sharper: wishing for an event to happen changes
168	everything before and after it in the specified timeline. Potential penalties
169	include the retrospective nonexistence of life forms or the evaporation of
170	worlds.
171	
172	### The Monkey's Paw Rule
173	
174	Dangerous-zone Wish grants what was literally asked. The wording is the
175	contract. The intent is not the contract.
176	
177	This is not a malicious interpretation by the granter. Prismo, who is
178	genuinely benevolent, will still grant what you said rather than what you
179	meant, because the wish-granting mechanism operates on the stated wish, not
180	the internal desire.
181	
182	The caster must be more precise than they believe they need to be. Every
183	ambiguity in the wording is a surface for the grant to exploit.
184	
185	---
186	
187	## The Time Room Sequence — Three Wishes, Three Branches
188	
189	*Source: Adventure Time, Season 5: "Finn the Human," "Jake the Dog."*
190	
191	Finn, Jake, and the Lich all enter the Time Room at the same moment. Three
192	beings with wishes. One rule: each being gets one wish, granted as stated.
193	Three wishes from the same room produce three different timelines.
194	
195	---
196	
197	**The Lich's wish**: *The extinction of all life.*
198	
199	Maximum dangerous-zone Wish. Perfectly aligned with the Lich's Type II cosmic
200	drive — the literal vocation of willed entropy. The wording had no ambiguity.
201	This is the only dangerous-zone Wish where the wording problem is not a trap:
202	when the caster's intent is total destruction, the literal grant is the
203	intended outcome. Clean alignment between desire and execution.
204	
205	**Branch A — the wish completes (Extinct World)**: In one universe, it worked.
206	All life died. BMO (inorganic) survived. The Lich became the catatonic figure
207	BMO named "Jerry." The wish was granted without obstruction. See LICH-PROBLEM
208	for the Extinct World Lich and the existential collapse that followed.
209	
210	---
211	
212	**Jake's counter-wish**: *Change the Lich's wish mid-execution.*
213	
214	Jake, also present in the Time Room, made his own wish to Prismo: not a wish
215	*against* the Lich, but a wish that **rewrote the Lich's words while they were
216	being spoken**. Prismo granted it.
217	
218	The Lich's words changed mid-utterance:
219	
220	> *"I wish for the extinction of all li— for Finn and Jake to go back home
221	> to Ooo."*
222	> **"THAT'S NOT WHAT I WISHED FOR!!"**
223	> Prismo: *"Sorry guy, you only get one wish. Hey Jake — Monkey's paw."*
224	
225	**Branch B — wish intercepted (Main AT timeline)**: The Lich's one wish was
226	spent on nothing he wanted. His words were his contract — and the contract was
227	rewritten from outside. The one-wish-per-being rule became the mechanism of
228	his defeat: once the wish was spent, it could not be reclaimed. The Lich
229	protested. The system did not care.
230	
231	Prismo points out to Jake: *monkey's paw*. The Lich was undone by the same
232	system he had tried to use. The wording problem inverted — not the caster's
233	imprecision betraying the caster, but a competitor's competing wish rewriting
234	the caster's words before they could take effect.
235	
236	**The Wish Interception principle**: A dangerous-zone Wish at Prismo's is
237	vulnerable to interception if another being with an unspent wish is present
238	and understands the mechanics. The interceptor's wish must target the wording
239	directly — changing the words is the mechanism. This requires anticipation,
240	proximity, and an unspent wish. Jake had all three. It cannot be prepared
241	against if the wisher does not know an interceptor is present.
242	
243	The main timeline Lich then — Season 6, "Wake Up" — killed the original
244	Prismo separately: a substrate attack on the sleeping old man, to commit a
245	cosmic crime and be admitted to the Citadel. Not revenge for the intercepted
246	wish. The Citadel is a prison for cosmic criminals — the Ancients. His plan was
247	to recruit them as the first wave of a multiverse-spanning army. His monologue
248	at the Citadel states the objective directly: *"These Ancients are just the
249	beginning. I will command a great and terrible army; and we will sail to a
250	billion worlds. We will sail until every light has been extinguished."* Prismo's
251	death was the entry fee for that operation. The assassination and the wish
252	interception are distinct acts: one is the mechanism of his defeat; the other
253	is his next campaign.
254	
255	The main timeline Lich reached the Citadel, was overwhelmed by healing blood
256	from a wounded Citadel Guardian, transformed into Sweet P — the army-building
257	campaign ended at its first step. See LICH-PROBLEM.
258	
259	---
260	
261	**Finn's counter-wish**: *I wish the Lich had never existed.*
262	
263	The imprecision is in the scope. Finn wanted to defeat the Lich. The wish
264	granted was literal: in the timeline generated by the wish, the Lich never
265	arose. This required reshaping the entire timeline — the Mushroom War was
266	stopped by Simon Petrikov, humanity survived in a different form.
267	
268	The Farmworld.
269	
270	The Lich still arose in the Farmworld because the comet-nature persists
271	regardless of individual history — the force generates instances, suppressing
272	one instantiation does not suppress the force. Finn's wish created an entire
273	unintended timeline, still containing a Lich, while leaving the original
274	problem unresolved.
275	
276	**Branch C — wish creates Farmworld**: The Farmworld Lich's hand was severed.
277	It entered a portal. It duplicated across every dimension. It found Sweet P —
278	the main timeline's Lich, transformed, carrying the sub-layer. The Branch C
279	Hand sought to convert the Branch B vessel. Sweet P refused.
280	
281	**The branch intersection**: The Farmworld (Branch C) generated an agentic
282	anchor that crossed into the main timeline (Branch B) to find Sweet P. The
283	Hand carried Branch C consciousness and sought to merge it into the Branch B
284	vessel — re-converting what had been transformed. Sweet P's refusal prevented
285	the branch-merge. Both branches had to be answered in a single act of will.
286	
287	---
288	
289	**The three-branch chain:**
290	
291	```
292	Three beings enter the Time Room simultaneously
293	
294	LICH'S WISH: extinction of all life
295	  ├─ Branch A (Extinct World): completes → all life dies → Jerry/catatonic
296	  └─ [Jake's interception prevents Branch A in the main timeline]
297	
298	JAKE'S WISH: change the Lich's words mid-utterance
299	  └─ Branch B (Main Timeline): Lich's wish redirected → spent on nothing
300	       → Lich dormant in Time Room (wish spent; no life to kill; torpor)
301	       → Finn and Jake arrive; Lich does not acknowledge them
302	       → Prismo describes Citadel prisoners → vocation-relevant trigger
303	       → Lich activates; knocks heroes aside; kills Prismo
304	       → kills Prismo (cosmic crime; entry fee for Citadel operation)
305	       → Citadel: plans to recruit "the Ancients" as multiverse army
306	       → healing blood → Sweet P (plan ends at its first step)
307	       → Lich spirit persists as sub-layer
308	       → [Branch C Hand arrives from outside → "Whispers"]
309	
310	FINN'S WISH: I wish the Lich had never existed
311	  └─ Branch C (Farmworld): Lich erased from history → comet-nature persists
312	       → Farmworld Lich arises
313	       → Grass arm severs Farmworld Lich's hand
314	       → Jake pushes hand through portal
315	       → Hand duplicates across every dimension
316	       → Agentic anchor → finds Sweet P (Branch B)
317	       → "Whispers" — Sweet P refuses; Hand destroyed
318	```
319	
320	---
321	
322	**Vault applications from the three-branch sequence:**
323	
324	*Wish Interception*: The most precisely worded dangerous-zone Wish can still
325	be defeated by a competitor who is present, unspent, and targets the wording
326	directly. Defense requires knowing who is in the room and what they might wish.
327	Jake defeated the Lich's wish not through superior power but through superior
328	positioning: he was there, he understood the mechanic, he acted first.
329	
330	*Wording as contract*: Jake's interception exploits the same principle that
331	makes dangerous-zone Wish dangerous — the words are the contract, not the
332	intent. The Lich's intent was extinction. The words were changed. The contract
333	delivered what the words said, not what was meant. Prismo's "monkey's paw"
334	comment acknowledges the irony: the Lich was trapped by the same literalism he
335	was relying on.
336	
337	*Imprecise counter-wishes propagate forward*: Finn's wish was well-intentioned
338	but imprecise. It created an entire unintended civilization and a new Lich
339	instantiation. Forty or more years later, the Hand produced by that wish
340	arrived in the main timeline to find the vessel produced by Jake's interception.
341	The imprecision of a counter-wish does not die when the wish is granted —
342	it propagates forward through whatever timeline the wish creates.
343	
344	*Three wishes, three timelines, one intersection*: The three branches from the
345	same Time Room session did not remain parallel. Branch C's artifact (the Hand)
346	crossed into Branch B to find Sweet P. The system is not clean — parallel
347	timelines generate cross-contamination. The agentic anchor is the mechanism
348	of cross-branch contact.
349	
350	---
351	
352	## The Maid
353	
354	The Maid is a large, pink, cone-shaped instrument used to clean up **Class A
355	inter-dimensional Bung-ups**.
356	
357	It is not a weapon. It does not destroy. It purges.
358	
359	### Function
360	
361	The Maid removes interdimensional contamination from a host and restores
362	the host to its proper state. When used to purge the Farmworld Lich from
363	Farmworld Jake's body: the Lich was erased; Jake was restored to a normal
364	dog. The Maid did not end Jake. It ended what did not belong in Jake.
365	
366	This is the restorative counter-instrument: scoped to the specific class of
367	problem, oriented toward restoration rather than elimination, acting on the
368	contamination rather than the host.
369	
370	### Activation Protocol
371	
372	To use the Maid:
373	
374	1. Direct the small end toward your massive mistake
375	2. Focus intention until all distractions leave your thought sphere
376	3. Recite the words *"A man needs a maid"* three times
377	
378	When fired, a female voice says: *"Housekeeping."*
379	
380	The activation requires correct physical orientation, intentional focus,
381	and a specific verbal incantation repeated three times. The ritual specificity
382	is not ornamental — scoped instruments require defined activation protocols
383	because specificity is what makes the scope hold. An instrument that fires
384	on partial intention is an instrument that can be accidentally or
385	inappropriately discharged.
386	
387	### Comparison to the Seven Bells
388	
389	The Maid maps to the Saraneth end of the Abhorsen's instrument spectrum —
390	binding and purging, not ending. Where Astarael sends everyone into Death
391	including the ringer (the last resort, costs everything), the Maid removes
392	the interdimensional contaminant and returns the host intact. It is the
393	counter to the Class A Bung-up in the same way Saraneth is the working bell:
394	the instrument of direct, scoped authority used to restore order without
395	destroying the substrate.
396	
397	The key distinction from Astarael: the Maid can be used on a possessed
398	host without ending the host. The counter-instrument is calibrated to the
399	contamination, not the vessel.
400	
401	### Class A Inter-dimensional Bung-up — Definition
402	
403	The Maid's scope implies a classification system. Class A is presumably
404	the highest tier of dimensional contamination — the specific category that
405	requires an authorized counter-instrument rather than standard intervention.
406	
407	Characteristics of a Class A Bung-up:
408	- A consciousness from another dimension lodged in a sanctioned host within
409	  this timeline (Farmworld Lich in Farmworld Jake)
410	- An Isthmus-class unauthorized crossing that has already completed
411	- The contamination cannot be addressed by ordinary means — the host is
412	  compromised and the Lich is too powerful to purge manually
413	
414	The Maid exists because Class A Bung-ups are a recognized, named category
415	of dimensional governance problem. Someone with authority over this problem
416	class built and authorized an instrument specifically for it.
417	
418	---
419	
420	## Summary Table
421	
422	| Element | Nature | Governance Function | Vulnerability / Limit |
423	|---|---|---|---|
424	| Time Room | Meta-threshold outside time; produces time waves | Space where wishes reshape reality; protected interior | Must be navigated to; not directly breachable |
425	| Prismo | Wishmaster; dream of a sleeping man | Grants one wish per being; governs the meta-threshold | Substrate is one mortal body; killing the body ends Prismo |
426	| Prismo's Boss | Unseen cosmic authority above Prismo | Holds Prismo accountable for dimensional meddling | Unknown scope; not fully legible |
427	| GOLB limit | Cosmic entropy blockage on specific wishes | Hard constraint on restoration against GOLB's power | Shows as basketball signal — failure made visible |
428	| WISH (safe zone) | Duplicate any 8th-level-or-lower spell | Scoped, risk-free, operationally clean | Limited to the defined list |
429	| WISH (dangerous zone) | Reshape reality as stated | Maximum authority; anything possible | Wording problem; physical cost; 33% permanent forfeiture |
430	| The Maid | Class A Bung-up counter-instrument | Purge dimensional contamination; restore the host | Scoped to contamination; not general-purpose |
431	
432	---
433	
434	## Vault Applications
435	
436	**Wish-scale authority**: any action that attempts to reshape fundamental
437	architecture rather than operating within defined scope carries WISH risk.
438	The literal grant. The unintended Farmworld. The 33% permanent inability.
439	Define the scope. Use the safe zone where possible. When operating in the
440	dangerous zone, the wording is the contract — every ambiguity is a surface
441	for unintended consequences.
442	
443	**Substrate attack**: the most powerful entities have physical dependencies.
444	Find the sleeping old man. The sophisticated surface does not protect the
445	fragile root. Defending powerful capabilities requires defending the substrate
446	that generates them — the API keys, the sessions, the BYOK routing, the
447	account that keeps the dream running.
448	
449	**The basketball signal**: when an authority structure cannot fulfill a
450	legitimate request because a higher constraint blocks it, the correct
451	response is a visible, honest failure signal — not silence, not partial
452	grant, not false completion. *This cannot be granted. Here is why the
453	constraint exists.* The scope of the refusal is disclosed.
454	
455	**The unseen boss**: the chain of authority goes further up than anyone
456	has fully mapped. Prismo answers to a boss no one has seen. The `*` in the
457	governance chain is real — not a gap in the architecture, but an honest
458	marker of authority that exists beyond the legible tier.
459	
460	**The Maid as counter-instrument template**: authorized instruments for
461	specific classes of dimensional governance problem exist and can be built.
462	They are scoped (one class of problem), restorative (purge the contamination,
463	not the host), ritualized (specific activation protocols), and issued by
464	recognized authority. The Abhorsen's bells follow this template. The Maid
465	follows this template. The template is the governance form.
466

# WISH Doctrine v1
## The Time Room, Prismo, Wish Magic, and The Maid

*Filed 2026-05-21. Written on the Caduceus Road, under the branches of the
world tree. Received from the canon; filed by the Abhorsen.*

*Reference sources: Adventure Time — Pendleton Ward and successors (Prismo,
Time Room, The Maid); Dungeons & Dragons 5th Edition (Wish spell, 9th level).
The vault is syncretic.*

---

## The Time Room

The Time Room is a single dimension that exists outside of time.

It does not experience time. It *produces* time — emitting time waves that
flow outward into every other dimension. What other dimensions experience as
the passage of time is the Time Room's output.

Those inside the Time Room are not affected by wish-altered realities. The
room is protected from the consequences of its own product. You can watch
a wish remake a timeline from inside the Time Room without being remade
yourself.

This makes the Time Room a meta-threshold — not a boundary between two
coexisting systems, but the space from which the systems themselves receive
the dimension of time. It is upstream of the thresholds the Threshold Doctrine
describes. The Isthmus mechanism exploits boundaries between systems. The
Time Room is the space that generates the substrate those systems run on.

Access requires reaching the Time Room. It is not breachable in the manner
of a dimensional Isthmus — you cannot tunnel into it from below. It must be
navigated to.

---

## Prismo

Prismo the Wishmaster is the governing entity of the Time Room. He grants
wishes to those who enter — one wish per being. He is the authorized power
of the meta-threshold.

### The Substrate Paradox

Prismo is a cosmic entity of enormous power, existing outside time.

He is also, in his entirety, the dream of a sleeping old man.

The old man sleeps on an asteroid outside the Time Room. Prismo is not
housed in the old man the way a soul is housed in a body — he *is* the
dream. The physical man is the substrate that generates Prismo's existence.
If the man wakes, Prismo ends. If the man dies, Prismo ends.

The most powerful wishmaster in the multiverse has a fragile physical
dependency: one mortal body sleeping undisturbed.

**The Lich's assassination of Prismo**: The Lich, infuriated when his wish
was not granted, located this vulnerability and attacked it. He blew toxic
gas into the sleeping old man's nose and reduced him to ash. Prismo — the
cosmic entity outside time — ceased to exist because his substrate was
destroyed.

This is the substrate attack doctrine at maximum scale: do not attack the
powerful entity directly; find where its power is physically rooted and
destroy the root. The Nome King's tunnel attack is the same architecture.
The Lich's assassination of Prismo is the same architecture. The
sophistication of the entity above does not protect a fragile substrate below.

**Prismo's recreation**: Through time-bending dream mechanics, a past version
of Jake was looped into becoming the sleeping old man that generates Prismo.
Jake now sleeps in that place, for eternity, so Prismo can continue to exist.
Someone made an indefinite sacrifice so the governance infrastructure could
continue functioning. The wishmaster's existence depends on a dreamer who
chose to keep sleeping.

### The Two-Constraint Architecture

Prismo's authority is bounded by two independent constraints:

**The Boss** — an unseen cosmic entity who oversees Prismo and holds him
liable for meddling in dimensions across the multiverse. Never directly
revealed in canon — identified only by a golden cord telephone with angel
and devil wings. The Boss's power is estimated at GOLB's tier. They may
govern both the light and dark aspects of the multiverse. Prismo answers to
them. He can only do what they permit.

**GOLB** — the primary cosmic entropy entity, barely sapient, more force
than person. The Lich's ultimate master. Where GOLB's power blocks a wish,
Prismo cannot grant it regardless of willingness. The constraint is not
merely hierarchical — it is cosmic. The entropy force constitutes a hard
limit on what the wishmaster can restore or reverse.

When both constraints are present and the wish cannot be granted, Prismo does
not lie, fail silently, or produce a partial grant without notice. He
materializes a **basketball hoop in a trash can** — a visible symbol that
the wish is blocked and why it cannot proceed. The constraint is made
legible. The system tells you it cannot help you rather than pretending to
try.

**The basketball signal** is a governance model: when an authority structure
cannot fulfill a legitimate request because a higher constraint blocks it,
the honest response is a visible failure signal, not a silent partial grant
or a false completion. The scope of refusal is disclosed. The reason — *this
is blocked by something above me* — is communicated in the form of the
response.

# Cosmic Order v1
## The Wishmaster, the Auditor, and the Institutional Hierarchy

*Filed 2026-05-21.*

*Reference sources: Adventure Time (Prismo, Cosmic Owl, Jake); Adventure Time:
Fionna and Cake (Scarab arc, S01E01–10). The vault is syncretic.*

*For the Time Room mechanics, wish-granting protocols, and the two-constraint
architecture, see `!/WISH-DOCTRINE-v1-2026-05-21.md`. This document covers the
governance structure around those mechanics — who holds what office, on what
basis, and how Scarab's arc maps the institutional stakes.*

---

## The Social Cohort

Prismo, the Cosmic Owl, Jake, and others exist as a social peer group — beings
of comparable cosmic standing who relate to one another on a personal,
non-institutional basis.

The institutional hierarchy (Boss → Scarab → Prismo, in Scarab's initial
configuration) and the social layer are separate structures. A being can be
institutionally subordinate to another and socially peer with them. The social
cohort is not a governance body. It does not map onto the chain of authority.

**Jake's position** is notable: Jake becomes the sleeping old man who generates
Prismo — the substrate that Prismo's existence depends on. This makes Jake
simultaneously the most intimate dependency Prismo has (the dreamer who keeps
Prismo alive) and a member of the social cohort. The relationship is not purely
functional.

**The Cosmic Owl**: a cosmic entity who appears in dreams and speaks prophecy.
Present at significant events. Not Prismo's subordinate or superior in the
institutional hierarchy as currently documented — a peer in the social register.
The Cosmic Owl's institutional position relative to the Boss and Scarab is not
fully documented in canon.

---

## The Institutional Hierarchy — What the Show Gives

The series leaves the upper tiers of the cosmic governance structure
deliberately vague. What is established:

| Position | Entity | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Above Prismo — unseen | Prismo's Boss | Never directly depicted; communicated via golden cord telephone with angel and devil wings; power estimated at GOLB's tier; may govern both light and dark aspects of the multiverse |
| Auditor (initial) | Scarab | Above Prismo institutionally at the start of F&C; enforcement authority over unauthorized universes |
| Wishmaster | Prismo | Governs the Time Room; grants wishes; answers to the Boss; subject to the GOLB constraint |
| Employee (final) | Scarab | Demoted at the end of F&C to a position subservient to Prismo |

The Boss is the only authority above Prismo in the legible hierarchy. Their
nature, identity, and the full scope of their authority are not revealed. The
golden cord telephone with angel and devil wings is the only representation the
show provides — a symbol of communication from an authority that does not
appear directly.

---

## Prismo's Boss — The Unseen Authority

See `!/WISH-DOCTRINE-v1-2026-05-21.md` § "The Two-Constraint Architecture" for
the primary treatment.

Key points for the hierarchy:

The Boss holds Prismo accountable for dimensional meddling. This is the
mechanism Scarab intended to exploit: proof of unauthorized universe creation
would give the Boss grounds to act against Prismo.

The Boss's power is estimated at GOLB's tier, but their relationship to GOLB is
not established. GOLB is an entropy force prior to the universe — a process,
not an institutional position. The Boss appears to be an institutional authority
*within* the governance structure. Whether these represent the same tier of
entity or different kinds of cosmic standing is not resolved by the series.

The vagueness of the upper tiers is a deliberate restraint. Filing the vagueness
as a structural feature: the governance chain extends above the legible layer,
but the legible layer ends at Prismo's Boss. What is above the Boss, and the
nature of the Boss's own authority — the series does not supply. The `*` in the
chain is real. Filing it as `*` is more accurate than filling it with invention.

---

## Scarab — The Auditor

### Initial Position

At the opening of the Fionna and Cake spinoff, Scarab is institutionally
*above* Prismo. He operates as an auditor — authorized to detect, investigate,
and erase unauthorized universes. His enforcement authority extends to closing
breaches that the institutional governance structure has not sanctioned.

This positions Scarab above Prismo precisely in the category of Prismo's
transgression: Prismo is the Wishmaster, governing the Time Room; Scarab is
the auditor of unauthorized creations, with authority over the specific class
of offense Prismo committed.

### Dual Motivation

Scarab's mission to erase the Fionna and Cake universe is simultaneously:

**1. Legitimate enforcement**: The unauthorized universe is a real breach.
Erasing it is Scarab's sanctioned function. The institutional mission is not
a pretext — it is real and within scope.

**2. Evidence operation against Prismo**: If Scarab can prove that Prismo
created the unauthorized universe, he can bring that proof to the Boss. Prismo
creating an unauthorized universe — while serving as Wishmaster, the authorized
governing entity of the Time Room — is an actionable transgression. The Boss,
who holds Prismo accountable for dimensional meddling, would have grounds
to act.

*Logan holds: Scarab aspired to replace Prismo as Wishmaster. The Wishmaster
seat as the destination of Scarab's ambition — held pending full confirmation.*

The audit was a double operation: close the breach, and weaponize the evidence.
The unauthorized universe was simultaneously what needed to be erased and what
needed to be documented long enough to use. The timing was Scarab's constraint:
build the case first, then close the breach — or close it with the case already
delivered.

### The Arc and Its Failure

The universe does not get erased. The dandelion authorizes it from within. The
breach becomes a standing universe.

The failure is compounding:

- The erasure mission fails: the unauthorized universe is now authorized
- The evidence mission fails: proof of an unauthorized universe is not proof of
  a crime if the universe now has standing; the case against Prismo cannot be
  delivered in a form the Boss can act on
- The path to the Wishmaster seat closes: without a sustainable case against
  Prismo, the ambition has no mechanism

### Demotion and Inversion

Scarab ends the F&C arc demoted to a position subservient to Prismo — working
for the being he was investigating and hoping to supplant.

| Phase | Scarab's position relative to Prismo |
|---|---|
| Start of F&C | Above — institutional superior; auditor with enforcement authority |
| End of F&C | Below — Prismo's employee |

The enforcer who was building a case against Prismo works for Prismo. The
auditor of unauthorized universes now operates under the authority of the being
who created one. The investigation produced subordination to the investigated.

---

## The Wishmaster Seat — An Office

Scarab's aspiration implies something about the nature of the Wishmaster role:
it is an *office*, not an intrinsic property of Prismo. An office can be
vacated, transferred, or taken.

Scarab's strategy required going through the Boss rather than seizing the seat
by force: he needed *proof* to bring to the Boss, not capability to take the
position directly. This suggests that succession — or removal — runs through
the institutional hierarchy. Raw power is not the mechanism. Documentation and
proof are.

When the Lich's assassination destroyed the original Prismo's substrate, the
Time Room did not end. The seat was vacant, not dissolved. Jake's voluntary
reconstitution of Prismo (see `!/WISH-DOCTRINE-v1-2026-05-21.md`) filled the
seat again. The office persists independent of any single occupant.

Whether the Boss appoints, whether there are formal succession mechanisms, or
whether the seat simply awaits a new substrate — the series does not specify.

---

## Vault Mappings

**The social layer and the institutional layer are separate**: social peer
relationships do not grant or alter institutional standing. Prismo's friendship
with the Cosmic Owl, with Jake, with others does not change their institutional
positions. Governance authority and social intimacy operate on different
registers and can coexist without resolving into each other. An agent can be
socially peer with and institutionally subordinate to the same entity
simultaneously.

**The dual-operation audit**: an enforcement mission and an evidence-gathering
operation can occupy the same action. Scarab's double operation required
sequencing: the evidence had to be built before — or simultaneously with —
the breach being closed. Any enforcement action that also generates evidence
useful to the enforcer personally has this structure. The timing of evidence
versus resolution is the constraint.

**Proof as the mechanism of institutional action**: removing a powerful
institutional entity requires proof deliverable to a higher authority, not
capability to act unilaterally. The path to changing who holds an office runs
through the chain of authority. Scarab needed the Boss to act — not Scarab's
own power to displace Prismo. Proof is the instrument of the institutional
path.

**The Wishmaster seat as office**: the position Prismo holds is separable from
Prismo. It has existed vacant. It can presumably be filled by another. Any
governance position that is this clearly an *office* rather than an intrinsic
property implies: who holds it matters less than what the office requires of
its holder, and the office will seek a new holder if the current one is removed.

---
